clue.text: Performs in musical with key lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a letter moves it higher up the column, so it now comes first

explanation.surface: A performer in a musical whose song has been transposed up a key.
explanation.walkthrough: The key A in CATS is moved up to the top of the column, giving ACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to perform on stage, so 'acts' and 'performs' are matching verb forms.

clue.text: Table of maxima – their index, not their contents

indicators.note: leaving out what is inside each word keeps only its two ends

blocks.note: first and last letters of maxima
first and last letters of their
first and last letters of index

explanation.surface: A mathematician's note on tabulating maximum values by their index rather than the values themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word in 'maxima – their index' is emptied, not just 'index' as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers or data arranged in rows and columns, which is a table.

clue.text: It's taken before dressing with mixed herb – so what?

indicators.note: mixed letters have been stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: Sounds like a salad dressing recipe with herbs, shrugged off with 'so what?'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests salad, but here it means putting on clothes after washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower bath is a wash under a spray, which people take before getting clothed.

clue.text: Secret order caught copper over limit, initially getting time

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for order, as in OM, Order of Merit
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A police officer from a secret society nicked for speeding and given jail time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal; 'over limit' sounds like speeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult means hidden or esoteric, known only to initiates, so it is a synonym of secret.

clue.text: Rock 'n' Roll dad, housekeeper

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, disturbing the order of what follows

explanation.surface: A rock 'n' roll father who also does the housework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock 'n' Roll' reads as a music genre; only 'Rock' is the signal, and the 'n' joins the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord keeps a house, either one that is let to tenants or a pub, so 'housekeeper' fits cryptically.

clue.text: Ballas, Revel Horwood, Du Beke and Mabuse initially make a racket!

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letters, here of the four people's first names, joined in order

blocks.note: Shirley Ballas, head judge of Strictly Come Dancing

explanation.surface: The four Strictly Come Dancing judges all start shouting at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is the BBC's celebrity ballroom show; only the judges' surnames are printed, so the solver supplies Shirley, Craig, Anton and Motsi.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a fraudulent scheme, and a scam is exactly that kind of swindle.

clue.text: Showed cold symptoms and, having displaced fever initially by force, got cosy

indicators.note: displacing one thing by another swaps it out wherever it occurs
initially takes the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: breathed noisily through a blocked nose
g is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold and a fever who tucked themselves up warm.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Fs in SNUFFLED become Gs, giving SNUGGLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuggle is to settle into a warm, comfortable position, so snuggled means got cosy.

clue.text: Clap kids with no limits set

indicators.note: without their limits the words lose their first and last letters

explanation.surface: Applauding children without any restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid and set are both past participles meaning put down in place, as a table is laid or set.

clue.text: Repeat of tea dance

indicators.note: a repeat here means the same word is used several times in a row

blocks.note: cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A second outing for a tea dance, an afternoon social with refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is old British slang for tea, from Chinese; three of them make the Latin dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Cuban ballroom dance, one of the Latin styles on Strictly.

clue.text: State follows Conservative line, taking steps

indicators.note: follows puts the first-named piece after the second one

blocks.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a US state

explanation.surface: A state government toeing the Conservative party line and acting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' looks like a party line in the surface but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A conga is a dance performed in a single line, each person holding the one in front while stepping.

clue.text: One's driven by double-cross

blocks.note: first meaning: a fastener turned into wood with a driver
second meaning: to cheat or betray someone

explanation.surface: Someone motivated by betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw is a fastener driven in by a screwdriver, and to screw someone is slang for cheating them.

clue.text: Showing extract, found a mage dancing with sound

indicators.note: an extract is a piece cut out of a longer text, here out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across these four words

explanation.surface: A film clip of a wizard who turned up dancing to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With sound' reads like a soundtrack; 'sound' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound means in good condition, unharmed, which is what undamaged says.

clue.text: Dance: it's located a couple in front of hotel

definitions.text: it's located a couple in front of hotel

blocks.clueFragment: it's located a couple in front of hotel
blocks.note: second meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet this code word sits two places before Hotel

explanation.surface: A dance venue described as two doors down from a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO alphabet F, G and H are Foxtrot, Golf and Hotel, so F is two before H.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxtrot is a smooth ballroom dance and also the radio code word for the letter F.

clue.text: Foreign capital in candid report

indicators.note: a report is something spoken and heard, so the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: An honest news story about a foreign capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city such as Paris, but here it means money.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and is still used by Switzerland, so it is foreign money.

clue.text: As colour is applied, wiping a circle about the mouth

indicators.note: wiping something off removes it
applied like paint, the letters are spread around into a new arrangement

blocks.note: a circle has the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Lipstick being put on, wiping a ring around the lips.
explanation.walkthrough: One O comes out of AS COLOUR before the remaining seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscular relates to the mouth or to kissing, from the Latin osculum, little mouth.

clue.text: Strictly Come Dancing, with first of personalities on telly

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the following word
dancing letters move around and change places

explanation.surface: The BBC show Strictly Come Dancing, with its celebrity contestants on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The show's title is split: 'Strictly' is the definition and 'Dancing' stirs up the letters of 'Come'.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictly can mean absolutely or entirely, as in strictly forbidden, a synonym of completely.

clue.text: Spooner's last to show sign of hesitation: Boatman lifted in dance

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of the name before it
in a down clue lifting a word makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: um is the sound of hesitating
an AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor; Boatman is also the setter's name

explanation.surface: The setter hoisted aloft mid-dance, with a hesitant pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' promises a spoonerism, but only the last letter of the name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban dance and one of the Latin ballroom styles.

clue.text: Puzzled? Boatman might be

blocks.note: first meaning: confused, out of one's depth
second meaning: out on the ocean, as a sailor would be

explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter's own pseudonym, so the clue also jokes about the setter being lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both bewildered and literally on the open ocean, where a sailor spends time.

clue.text: One hiding on board tug, one overwhelmed by wave

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed and surrounded by what follows

blocks.note: to wave is to sway to and fro

explanation.surface: A man hiding on a tugboat swamped by a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tug' looks like a boat in the surface but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway is someone who hides aboard a ship or plane to travel without paying.

clue.text: Tot cycling with guardian

indicators.note: cycling moves the end letter round to the front

blocks.note: to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A toddler riding a bike with a parent watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child but is the verb meaning to add.
explanation.definitionFit: A father is a child's guardian, so dad stands for guardian by example.

clue.text: Separation is central to posture in Foxtrot, perhaps

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter
in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: the foxtrot is an example of a dance

explanation.surface: Keeping a gap between partners is key to the stance in a foxtrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posture' seems to mean STANCE whole, but only its central letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance is the space or gap between two things, so it means separation.

clue.text: Either way, one keeps house

indicators.note: either way says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

blocks.note: a woman who runs a household, and the title of a brothel-keeper

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, someone runs the household.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides a wink: a madam also keeps a house of ill repute.
explanation.definitionFit: A madam is a woman in charge of a household, and also one who runs a brothel.

clue.text: Ran out of funny Charleston costume

indicators.note: out of takes the first word's letters away from the next
funny means peculiar, so the letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A dancer who ran out of an amusing Charleston costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Costume' looks like the thing being run out of, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes and costume both mean the garments a person wears.

clue.text: It's used by a keyboardist to select a partial inversion

indicators.note: an inversion turns letters back to front, and partial says only some of them

explanation.surface: A musician picking out an inverted chord on the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first five letters of SELECTA are turned round; TA stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: The celesta is a keyboard instrument with hammers striking metal plates, as in the Sugar Plum Fairy.

clue.text: Claudia gutted over error: no risks taken here

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: a sin is a moral error

explanation.surface: Claudia, upset at a mistake, decides to play it safe.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places CA above SIN; the surface's 'no risks taken' hides that 'no' is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a gambling house, a place where people take chances with money.

clue.text: Argentine Tango: even parts of it can be read symbolically

definitions.text: Tango: even parts of it can be read symbolically

blocks.note: first meaning: silvery, from Latin argentum

blocks.clueFragment: Tango: even parts of it can be read symbolically
blocks.note: second meaning: the second and fourth letters of tango read as a chemical symbol for the metal

explanation.surface: A dancer's notes on the Argentine tango and its symbolism.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of tAnGo are A and G, and Ag is the chemical symbol for this metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentine as an adjective means of or like silver, from the Latin argentum.

clue.text: Settings for plates of say fish, pork and beef but not sheep's heart

indicators.note: say asks for a word spoken, taken by its sound rather than spelling
but not removes what follows from the piece before
'heart' keeps only the middle letter of 'sheep'

explanation.surface: A menu of fish, pork and beef, with sheep's heart off the list.
explanation.walkthrough: Plaice is a flatfish; heart means the middle letter, and sheep has five letters with E in the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Place mats are protective pads set at each diner's place at the table for plates to rest on.

clue.text: Plans hop-skip steps for dance

definitions.note: the answer is the first word of paso doble

indicators.note: hopping and skipping passes over every other letter

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Choreographing hops and skips for a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: The paso doble, Spanish for double step, is a Latin ballroom dance; paso alone is used for it.

clue.text: Some achieve Samba days before

indicators.note: some means a part of the following words, not all of them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Some dancers nail the samba a few days before the show.
explanation.definitionFit: An eve is the day before a special occasion, such as Christmas Eve.

clue.text: Equalises score: taking on Latin, they cover the floor

indicators.note: taking something on means admitting it inside

blocks.note: a tie is an equal score
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A dance couple level the scores with a Latin round and fill the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiles are flat slabs laid to cover floors and walls.

clue.text: Tess represented series

indicators.note: represented means shown again in a new form

explanation.surface: Tess Daly, Strictly presenter, fronted the television series.
explanation.walkthrough: Tess Daly co-hosts Strictly Come Dancing, fitting the dance theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a series of things belonging together, as in a set of matches in tennis.

clue.text: Uncovered belly-button on return of American Smooth

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word reads backwards
uncovering strips the outer letters off, keeping the middle

blocks.note: navel without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A costume showing a bare midriff for the American Smooth, a Strictly ballroom dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American Smooth' reads as one dance name; 'American' is wordplay and 'Smooth' the definition. The belly-button is the navel.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave means smoothly charming and polished in manner.

clue.text: Uniting against virus: hospital department

blocks.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
ENT is ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: Everyone pulling together against a flu outbreak in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Confluent describes streams flowing together, merging into one, so it means uniting.
